fixes.explanation: Good guess, since Jesus does teach. Mark 6:34 says He began to teach the crowd many things. But here the people beg Him to touch the man (Mark 8:22). They brought a blind man, so they came asking for a touch. Teaching is a fine thing, just not what this verse says.
Baptize is a big word, and it's not in this verse. The people beg Jesus to touch the blind man (Mark 8:22). The verse doesn't mention water at all. I'd have loved a splash, but the text says touch.

I get the guess, but the verse doesn't say that. Jesus leads the blind man by the hand out of the village (Mark 8:23). No shoreline, no boats, just a walk out of the village. Keep the sea out of this one.

John 9:7 has a man told to wash in the pool of Siloam, but that's a different story. Here, Jesus places His hands on the man's eyes again (Mark 8:25). No washing in this one. Jesus stays right there with him.
Nope, no coming back later. Jesus places His hands on the man's eyes once again (Mark 8:25). The man isn't sent away to return another day. I'd stay put, too, friend.

I see why you'd pause, since the man said the people looked like trees walking around (Mark 8:24). But the text says his sight was restored, and he could see everything clearly (Mark 8:25). So this one is true. Trees walking around are behind him now.
